name: Battlezone

P4.note: data bus transceiver; AM83048 alternate with different pin numbering

L2.note: ROM0 and ROM1 selects; same package as the 03A address-selector gate

K5.note: VGRST, WDCLR, VGGO, COINCK, OPT0/1, SINP

P2.note: second bus transceiver; DB0-7 pulled up by resistors R1-R6; AM8304B alternate with different pin numbering

R125.note: DATA DISABLE pull-up; DATA DISABLE and M7 feed J4 to make DATA ENABLE

L4.note: clocked at 3KHZ, held by TEST, carry out through K2 to NMI -- self-test changes the NMI rate

L/M1.note: spans L1 and M1; selected by ROM4

F/H1.note: spans F1 and H1; selected by ROM1

SW1.note: on-board RESET switch, pulled up by 10k with a 1N914 clamp and 1uF, into two LS14 stages at B6

WDDIS.note: watchdog disable; a board that resets every few seconds and a board with this jumper fitted look nothing alike on the bench

Y1.note: alternate circuit, drawn dashed, with two P5 (74S04) inverters and 330R bias

Y2.note: main circuit, with Q1 (2N3904), L1 (100uH), 39pF/100pF and a 10k/10k divider

Q1.note: oscillator transistor for the Y2 circuit

VR2.note: +5VDAC from the same +22VDC, clamped by CR11 (1N100)

CR2.note: +5V present indicator through a 150R -- the first thing to look at on a dead board

R11.note: DIAG STEP, SELF-TEST, SLAM, coin switches, 3KHZ, HALT

J6.note: stack pointer up/down counter; STROB1, DISRST, OP1, OP2

E6.note: register file, AVG9-12; carries WA/RA/WB/RB and GR/GW

RP1.note: fitted only when 74LS170 is used in place of 74LS670

RP2.note: fitted only when 74LS170 is used in place of 74LS670

D4.note: AB11/12 vs AVG11/12 -> AM11/AM12; also gates VW and BUFFEN

C4.note: second half of the 02A decoder; AM11/AM12 -> VROM1, VROM2, VROM3

A3.note: mask ROM; 2708 alternate needs the split pads recut

B/C3.note: spans B3 and C3; 2708 alternate needs the split pads recut

F/H3.note: spans F3 and H3; selected by VROM2M

F2.note: DVG0-7 <-> DB0-7; AM8304B alternate with different pin numbering. DVG0-7 are pulled up by resistors R10-R17 (10k) -- resistors, not the ICs at grid positions R10 and R11

C6.note: NORM gated against LATCH0-LATCH3 for the shift-register mode inputs

B6.note: LATCH0-LATCH3 inverters; same package as the 02A watchdog

K8.note: DVY12 and OP0/OP1/OP2, clocked by LATCH1

L10.note: second flip-flop of the 02A watchdog package; VGCK from 6MHZ

M7.note: cross-coupled latch; same package as the 02A DATA ENABLE gate

R9.note: SCALELD inverter; same package as the 02B option-switch enables

N8.note: CNTR latch; STOP and HALT inputs

L5.note: K6CO/L6CO combining; also the DISRST gate in the halt latch

J4.note: OP1 term; same package as the 02A watchdog gate

K4.note: KGCO/LGCO -> STOP; same package as the 02A address decode gate

K7.note: Atari 036408 vector state PROM; OP0/OP1/OP2 in, STATE0-STATE3 out

M9.note: AVG0 from STATE2 in the first half; the second half is the vector halt latch (HALT set from OP0 by STROBE3, cleared by VGGO)

notes: Two 12.096 MHz crystals (Y1, Y2) with an alternate clock circuit drawn dashed — the board was built both ways.
Clock tree: 12MHz -> N4 (74193) -> 6/3/1.5MHz, and N5 (LS393) -> 3kHz/12kHz. E3MHZ and E6MHZ are gated through P8.
Same MPU as Asteroids — Atari 90-6013 (6502A) — and the same LS245/AM8304B transceiver substitution with alternate pin numbering.
A 50-pin test connector is fitted, marked 'FOR ATARI MANUFACTURING ONLY', bringing out the full address and data bus plus DATA DISABLE.
J19 (24-pin) carries the buffered bus to the Auxiliary Math Box PCB: EDB0-7, EAB0-6, ER/WB, EI/O, EPHI2 and the E6MHZ/E12KHZ/E3MHZ clocks.
Decode chain: M2 splits program/vector memory, C4 selects RAM vs I/O, K5 fans out to VGRST, WDCLR, VGGO, COINCK, OPT0/1 and SINP.

Two 8-position option switch banks: M10 (read by N11 via OPT0) and P10 (read by P11 via OPT1), both pulled up through 10k. R11 carries the coin door inputs plus 3KHZ and HALT, so a machine that will not coin up and one that reports the wrong vector-generator state share a buffer.

Sheet 3 Side A is the whole digital vector generator, and it is a section of the same 035742-01/-02 game PCB as sheet 2 -- so the designators share one grid. Several packages appear on both sheets using different halves: C4 (LS139), L10 (LS74), M7 (LS02), J4 (LS00), K4 (LS10), B6 (LS14), R9 (S04), K2 (S04).

Vector state PROM is K7, an 82S129 carrying Atari part 036408. OP0/OP1/OP2 address it and STATE0-STATE3 come out, so a vector generator stuck in one state points at K7, L7 (LS174 state register) or J7 (LS42 strobe/latch decoder) before anything else.

HALT is latched at M9 from OP0 by STROBE3 and cleared by VGGO, with DISRST from L5 combining RESET and VGRST. That same HALT is what the 02B coin-door buffer R11 reads back, so the self-test HALT indication and the vector generator's own halt are the same signal.
Vector-generator RAM is eight 2114s (Atari 90-7033) at A1-D1 and A2-D2, chip-selected in pairs from VRAM0, VRAM1, VRAM2/VROM1L and VRAM3/VROM1M.

Vector-generator ROM is four 8316E mask ROMs at A3, B/C3, E3 and F/H3 -- two of them drawn spanning two grid positions. 2708s can be fitted instead, but the drawing says that needs open pads bridged and connected pads cut in three places.

Two substitutions on this sheet change the parts fitted, not just the marking: 74LS170 in place of 74LS670 in the stack register file requires resistor packs RP1/RP2 to be installed, and AM8304B in place of 74LS245 at F2 renumbers every pin.

Program memory is six 8316E mask ROMs on sheet 2 Side A at N1, L/M1, K1, J1, F/H1 and E1, selected by ROM5 down to ROM0 in that left-to-right order. Two of them are drawn spanning two grid positions, the same convention the vector ROMs use on sheet 3.

The board carries its own power regulation for the analog vector-generator PCB: VR3 (7815) and VR2 (7805) off +22VDC, VR1 (7915) off -22VDC, with CR2 (MV5053) as the +5V present LED. +5V, -5V and +12V arrive already regulated on the edge connector.

The 'P,R18', 'P,R27' and 'P,R67' annotations scattered across every sheet are pull-ups to +5V through 1k resistors R18, R20, R27 and R67 -- given on sheet 2 Side A in the Power Input block, and nowhere else.
SW1 is an on-board reset pushbutton, and WDDIS is a watchdog-disable jumper. Both change how a board behaves before any fault is involved, so both are worth checking before chasing a reset loop.
conflicts: Designator namespace collision: on these sheets R9, R10 and R11 are ICs at those grid positions (R9 is a 74S04, R10/R11 are 74LS244s on sheet 2 Side B) and are also ordinary resistor numbers on sheet 2 Side A (R9 and R19 are the 10k pull-ups on the LS244 enables) and sheet 3 Side A (R10-R17 are the data-buffer pull-ups). Nothing on the drawing distinguishes them but the symbol: ICs are boxes or gates with a part number beneath, resistors are zigzags with a value. Not resolvable by renaming -- it has to be read off the symbol every time.

The map shows four vector-generator ROM positions — A3, B/C3, E3 and F/H3 — and MAME's Battlezone dumps populate only two of them, A3 and B/C3. Both Red Baron sets are the same. So E3 and F/H3 are positions the drawing shows and the board has 24-contact sockets for, but that these games appear to leave empty. Worth knowing before someone chases a missing chip that was never fitted. MAME confirms every other ROM and PROM position on this board exactly, including the 82S129 at K7 and the 82S123 at B1 on the Auxiliary PCB.
corrections: The LS245 alternate is AM8304B, not 'AM83048'. Read off both sheets: the sheet 2 Side A note spells out 'AM8304B INSTEAD OF 74LS245, 2 PLACES THIS PAGE', and sheet 3 Side A repeats it at F2. The two places on sheet 2 are P4 and P2 -- P2 was missing from the earlier read entirely.
The MPU's own designator on the sheet is 'L/M/N 3', not L3 -- it spans three grid positions, the same convention as the L/M1 and F/H1 ROMs and the B/C3 and F/H3 vector ROMs. Recorded here under L3.
